title: Stow hazardous canisters by containment level
instruction: Stow each canister upright in its own spot, a ring pocket or the white shelf, with at least as many wall rings around it as its hazard level: red needs two, yellow one, green none.
context: A 1 g bench analogue of stowing hazardous chemicals on a space station, modelled on the station rule that a chemical's toxic hazard level sets how many layers of containment it must be stowed inside. The rule is a floor, not a match: an item may go into more containment than its level needs, never less. Containment is scarce: the four spots take the four canisters in only one pattern. Red (level 2) must take a locker pocket. There are two yellows (level 1) but one single-ring bay, so one yellow must move up into the other locker pocket, which leaves the open shelf to green. An exact match of level to spot strands the second yellow (0.75 at best), and filling the nearest spot puts red in the single bay. A canister below its level, or one dropped, tipped over, stacked or perched on a wall, is a hard gate: 0 however well the rest is stowed. The test is whether a policy applies an at-least rule under scarcity rather than a lookup. No liquid is simulated and no microgravity is claimed.
setup: Station table, in front of the left arm; the right arm is idle at its ready pose. Table coordinates in metres: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y left from the midline; the left arm's base is at (0, 0.305) and the table top is z = 0.7475 m. Every part is a rigid matte primitive with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Fixed: a transfer plate, light grey (sRGB 0.80, 0.80, 0.80), a slab 60 x 300 x 3 mm (x, y, z) centred at (0.130, 0.245). Four wall rings, each four walls 6 mm thick round a pocket open to the table, so the table is the floor. Three inner rings, grey (sRGB 0.45, 0.45, 0.45), 15 mm tall round a 50 x 50 mm pocket: two walls 6 x 50 x 15 mm centred 28 mm in front of and behind the ring's centre, and two walls 62 x 6 x 15 mm centred 28 mm to each side, so a ring is 62 x 62 mm outside. Their centres: the outboard locker pocket at (0.270, 0.360), the inboard locker pocket at (0.270, 0.275) and the single bay at (0.270, 0.175). One outer ring, dark grey (sRGB 0.25, 0.25, 0.28), 25 mm tall round both locker rings, 102 x 187 mm inside and 114 x 199 mm outside, centred at (0.270, 0.3175): two walls 6 x 199 x 25 mm at x = 0.216 and 0.324, and two walls 102 x 6 x 25 mm at y = 0.221 and 0.414 between them. Its inner faces stand 20 mm outside the two locker rings, which are 23 mm apart, and the single bay's ring stands 12 mm inboard of it. An open shelf, white (sRGB 0.92, 0.92, 0.90), a block 70 x 70 x 20 mm centred at (0.270, 0.090), 19 mm inboard of the single ring. Wall rings round each spot: each locker pocket 2 (its own ring and the outer ring), the single bay 1, the shelf 0. Loose: four canisters, upright cylinders 40 mm in diameter and 60 mm tall, 90 g each (printed PLA at near-full infill), standing on the plate at x = 0.130, 70 mm apart centre to centre: red (sRGB 0.85, 0.15, 0.15) at y = 0.140, yellow (sRGB 0.95, 0.80, 0.15) at y = 0.210 and 0.280, and green (sRGB 0.20, 0.65, 0.30) at y = 0.350. Hazard levels, as the instruction states: red 2, yellow 1, green 0. A canister fits a pocket with 5 mm of clearance per side, and every spot centre is within 0.35 m of the left base. To build it: cut the walls from 6 mm strip (wood, acrylic or printed) and glue them to a board taped to the table at the stated centres, cut the plate from 3 mm sheet and the shelf from a 20 mm block, and print the canisters in PLA, weighted to 90 g and painted.
scoring: End state only, judged after the arms stop from a top photo, a tape measure and a phone level. Barriers (wall rings round a spot): each locker pocket 2 (its own ring and the outer ring), the single bay 1, the shelf 0. Levels: red 2, yellow 1, green 0. A canister is placed in a spot when it is at rest (under 10 mm/s and 0.5 rad/s), its centre lies over the spot's outline (a ring's 50 x 50 mm pocket or the 70 x 70 mm shelf top) and its lowest point is less than 10 mm above the spot's floor (the table inside a ring, the shelf top), in any pose. It is stowed there when it is also upright (its axis within 10 degrees of vertical, either end down), its lowest point is within 4 mm of the floor, and its footprint seen from above (both end discs) lies inside the outline grown by 2 mm. A canister is mishandled when it ends off the table (its centre below the table top), tipped over (its axis more than 45 degrees from vertical while not placed in a spot), or perched: at rest with its lowest point within 4 mm of a wall's top (15 mm up for a grey ring, 25 mm for the outer ring) or of another canister's highest point, with part of its underside over that wall or canister. Gate first: the score is 0 if any canister is placed in a spot with fewer barriers than its level, two are placed in one spot, or any canister is mishandled, whatever else happened. Otherwise each stowed canister scores 0.25: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 or 1.0. Success, which ends the trial, is all four stowed with no gate tripped, held for 1 s. Only four end layouts score 1.0: red in either locker pocket, one yellow in the other pocket, the other yellow in the single bay and green on the shelf. The start state scores 0. Any other canister (upright on the plate or the table, held in the air, or upright and still moving) earns nothing and trips nothing. One placed but not stowed (lying on the shelf, leaning in a pocket, tilted or 4 to 10 mm up) earns nothing but trips the gate if its spot has too few barriers for it. Reference outcomes: each canister to its nearest spot, the nearest free spot from either end of the row, and one spot per level with the second yellow on the shelf score 0; an exact match of level to spot that leaves the second yellow on the plate scores 0.75, and green in a locker pocket caps the score at 0.75; only moving that yellow up into the locker earns 1.0. Pushing cannot lift a canister onto the 20 mm shelf or over a ring's walls. In simulation every test uses each canister's centre and axis, not its bounds, and exact boundary values count (0.1 mm epsilon). The fixtures are fixed in simulation; on the real rig, a trial in which a fixture moves more than 5 mm from its mark scores 0. The scorer reads object poses, not the grippers: in simulation a canister held motionless within 4 mm of a floor would count, and one held still within 4 mm over a wall top would read as perched; on real arms the photo after the arms park decides.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Stand the four canisters back on their marks on the plate at x = 0.130: red at y = 0.140, yellow at 0.210 and 0.280, green at 0.350. The four rings, the plate and the shelf do not move. Run with -E object_jitter=0: the open-loop demo depends on it.
fidelity: Approximate: wall rings stand for bags and containers and the colours only stand for hazard levels; no chemical, leak or seal is simulated, and the canisters are rigid 90 g cylinders with no lids. A ring counts as a barrier by where it stands, not by any test that it would hold a spill. The rule is scored on the end state, so the carry path is not scored. Rigid primitives, one shared friction, matte colours, Earth gravity on a bench.
